source.title: Also for k-means: more data does not imply better performance
source.authors: M. Loog; Jesse H. Krijthe; M. Bicego

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper gives theoretical results on whether expected test risk can worsen as training sample size increases, using idealized k-means rather than the original deep-network settings.
record.gate_note: The paper cites double descent and prior nonmonotonic learning-curve results, but those cited findings are not its own results. Its own results test sample-size monotonicity for k-means; it does not test model size, training epochs, or an interpolation threshold.
record.test_reason: The paper proves that globally optimal 2-means can have expected test risk rise from N to N+1 samples, for every N ≥ 14. This is sample-wise nonmonotonicity, but it is not tied to an interpolation threshold. A 2-means learner fits its training set exactly only when N ≤ 2 distinct points are present, so N ≥ 14 lies far past any such point. The construction relies on ERM over a three-point distribution, not on interpolation, so it does not bear on V3's claim that more data hurts near the interpolation threshold. Double descent appears only in the paper's framing and discussion. No model-size, epoch, capacity, complexity-measure, noise or regularization result is given.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors prove 1-means is globally monotonic and 2-means is not even weakly monotonic (nonmonotonicity for every N ≥ 14), and leave k > 2 open. They also conjecture the result carries over to continuous distributions. They speculate that suboptimal practical k-means optimization may regularize the curve toward monotonicity.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses theoretical constructions for idealized, globally optimal ERM k-means with within-group squared loss. It does not reproduce deep-network double descent or sweep model capacity.
record.method_sensitivity: For the nonmonotonicity result, the constructed distribution can vary with each (N, N+1) pair; the proof uses a discrete three-point distribution.

fits_no_version.finding: Globally optimal ERM 2-means is not even weakly monotonic. For every N ≥ 14 there is a three-point distribution on which expected within-group squared risk rises from N to N+1.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Expected test risk of ERM learners (here 2-means clustering) can increase with sample size at arbitrarily large N, independent of any interpolation threshold.

fits_no_version.finding: 1-means (the sample mean) is globally monotonic in expected within-group squared risk.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For the idealized 1-means learner, expected within-group squared risk never increases with sample size when the risk difference exists.

record.problems: The evidence is theoretical and concerns idealized globally optimal k-means rather than practical optimization or deep networks. The 2-means construction is distribution-specific and may change with N; the paper does not establish a full fall-rise-fall curve or proximity to an interpolation threshold.
record.rows_left_out: No additional own results bearing on the tested version were reported. Results cited from other studies were excluded.

untested.parts: Model-size double descent in deep networks.
Sample-wise harm near an interpolation threshold. The study's harm occurs far from interpolation and gives no fall-rise-fall curve.
Capacity-wise second descent past interpolation across model classes.
Noise or regularization dependence, and multiple peaks. Regularization is only speculated about in the discussion.

record.verdict_notes: The reader linked r1 to V3 with a 'supports' verdict. I removed it because V3 specifies harm near the interpolation threshold, and this study's harm is unrelated to interpolation. A reviewer who reads V3 more broadly, as 'more data can hurt', might treat r1 as a T3 extension. Even then it would show harm outside the threshold condition, not confirm V3 as stated.

versions.untested_parts: Model-size double descent in deep networks.
The results do not locate the deterioration near an interpolation threshold or establish a complete fall-rise-fall curve.
Capacity-wise double descent across model classes and behavior past an interpolation point.
A single effective-complexity measure predicting peak location.
Noise or regularization dependence, multiple peaks, and disappearance under optimally tuned regularization.
Recounting complexity by effective parameters to assess whether the curve becomes U-shaped.

rows.subject: A_2 (2-means)
rows.operation_detail: Theoretically compares expected risk at training sample sizes N and N+1 under constructed distributions.

conditions.value: For each N, a constructed three-point distribution in one-dimensional feature space; the distribution may differ for each (N, N+1) pair.

rows.measure: Difference in expected risk, Δ_N^{N+1} = E(N) − E(N+1)
rows.baseline: E(N), expected risk at sample size N
rows.note: The theorem establishes existence of a distribution for every N ≥ 14; it does not report a numerical risk value or a full learning curve.
rows.check: Unlink from V3. The risk increase is shown for N ≥ 14 with k = 2, far from any interpolation threshold (exact fit needs N ≤ 2 distinct points). It is ERM nonmonotonicity, not threshold-driven deterioration. The result is an existence proof over a distribution chosen separately for each N, with no numeric risk values.

rows.subject: A_1 (1-means)
rows.operation_detail: Theoretically compares expected risk as training sample size increases.

conditions.value: Any distribution on ℝ^d for which the expected-risk difference exists

rows.baseline: Expected risk at sample size N+1
rows.value: Δ_N^{N+1} ≥ 0; the paper proves global monotonicity of 1-means
rows.note: This is a contrasting result for 1-means, not evidence about deterioration near an interpolation threshold.
rows.check: Unlink is correct: this is a monotonicity proof for 1-means, with no version link. The baseline wording is inverted: Δ compares E(N) against E(N+1), so the baseline is E(N).

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.condition: Globally optimal 2-means on the constructed three-point distributions, for every N ≥ 14
